t:
Section 5(t) of the Home Owners’ Loan Act (12 U.S.C. 1464(t)) is amended—
    (1) by striking paragraph (4) and inserting the following:“(4) [Repealed].”; and 
    (2) in paragraph (9)(A), by striking “intangible assets, plus” and all that follows through the period at the end and inserting “intangible assets.”.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to the Home Owners' Loan Act, repealing one paragraph and trimming a definition concerning intangible assets. It provides for no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. There is no tempting participation language here at all.
fable.s: by striking paragraph (4) and inserting the following:“(4) [Repealed].”

opus.w: The section only makes technical edits to the Home Owners' Loan Act: it repeals one paragraph and trims a capital definition. It involves no one outside the federal government and creates no rulemaking, comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue. Nothing in it could reasonably be read as participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the Home Owners' Loan Act, specifically repealing a paragraph and modifying a definition regarding intangible assets. It does not establish any advisory committees, public comment periods, consultations with outside entities, or rights to sue. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: Section 5(t) of the Home Owners’ Loan Act (12 U.S.C. 1464(t)) is amended— (1) by striking paragraph (4) and inserting the following:“(4) [Repealed].”; and (2) in paragraph (9)(A), by striking “intangible assets, plus” and all that follows through the period at the end and inserting “intangible assets.”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that amending a statute could implicitly change participation requirements, but this section only modifies definitions and repeals a paragraph without introducing any new consultation, hearing, or advisory mechanisms. It fails against the definition because it contains no language requiring interaction with outside parties.
